g1.flow: Ṭā Hā opens with wa: wa hal atāka ḥadīthu Mūsā, after 'To Him belong the best names', then Moses sees a fire. An-Nāziʿāt has plain hal, no wa, after 'suddenly they will be alert upon the earth's surface', then his Lord calls him in Ṭuwā. Hook: wa joins on to Allāh's names in Ṭā Hā; An-Nāziʿāt starts fresh.

cues.20:9: Ṭā Hā: wa hal, with wa; after 'To Him belong the best names'.
cues.79:15: An-Nāziʿāt: plain hal, no wa; after 'alert upon the earth's surface'.

g2.flow: Ṭā Hā has it twice. First idhhab (singular) to Moses, after 'Our greater signs'; he then asks for his breast to be expanded. Later idhhabā (both of you), after 'you and your brother', then 'speak to him gently'. An-Nāziʿāt has one idhhab, straight after the call in Ṭuwā, then 'would you purify yourself'. Hook: once the brother is named, the verb becomes dual.

cues.20:24: Ṭā Hā, 1st: idhhab (singular), after 'Our greater signs'; Moses asks for an expanded breast.
cues.20:43: Ṭā Hā, 2nd: idhhabā (both), after 'you and your brother'; next, gentle speech.
cues.79:17: An-Nāziʿāt: idhhab (singular), after the call in the sacred valley of Ṭuwā.

g3.flow: Identical words, matāʿan lakum wa li-anʿāmikum, closing a list of provisions in both. An-Nāziʿāt: after the mountains set firmly; next, 'the greatest Overwhelming Calamity'. ʿAbasa: after fruit and grass; next, 'the Deafening Blast'. Hook: mountains lead to the Calamity; fruit and grass lead to the Blast.

cues.79:33: An-Nāziʿāt: after 'the mountains He set firmly'; next, the greatest Overwhelming Calamity.
cues.80:32: ʿAbasa: after 'fruit and grass'; next, the Deafening Blast.
